symbol_renames.note: Symbol-level targets a repair moves TO, one row per documented mapping and never an inference -- the same contract package_renames carries, at member/type granularity. handler_parameters.note: Controller-method PARAMETER kinds the Spring Web compatibility extension documents (H6b). A 4xx the destination answers with an empty body where the source accepted the same request is the shape of a request refused before or at the handler boundary, and the planner (worklist.request_rejection_advice) resolves THIS handler's signature through the structure model against these rows. `undocumented` holds the kinds a Spring handler commonly declares that the list does not name; each row cites where its replacement is documented. Rows are documentation, never an inference about what the compat layer does with such a parameter -- the loop finds that. Each `undocumented` row carries an `action`: the one concrete first edit for a handler that declares that kind, phrased from the documentation the row cites and from nothing specific to any specimen; the planner renders it as the item's first action. When a unit seals such a kind and the compiler model shows it as the type of an HTTP handler parameter, the row's action is the unit's FIRST target, naming those handlers, ahead of any symbol_renames target for the same symbol; the rename then covers only the other uses (a helper's builder, a local) and names the handlers it is not for (V16-5: the bare rename left an unannotated UriBuilder the platform refused as a second request body).

org.springframework.web.util.UriComponen.action: the compat layer does not bind a UriComponentsBuilder: replace the parameter with @Context jakarta.ws.rs.core.UriInfo uriInfo and build the Location as uriInfo.getBaseUriBuilder().path(<the source's own path template>).build(<the source's own expansion arguments>) -- never new URI(String) (its checked URISyntaxException is vetoed) and never URI.create of a relative path (it drops the base the scenario compares). location_translation.rule: V17-5: the URI template expansion is translated argument by argument; the Location the source built, a null argument included, is the Location the destination builds
location_translation.null_argument: Spring UriComponentsBuilder.buildAndExpand expands a null value as an empty segment (201 with /api/x/); JAX-RS UriBuilder.build(Object...) throws IllegalArgumentException for a null value, so every argument the source did not pass as a non-null literal is passed null-tolerantly: `a == null ? location_translation.substitution: the argument stays the source's own expression (the same parameter, or a local of the same type, and the same accessors); another value -- typically the saved entity's id where the source expanded the request DTO's -- is a behaviour change unless decisions.yaml location_arguments.substitutions records it with an accepted ADR

write_calls.note: a source override is a WRITE when its recorded calls change persistent state through the JPA API (the effect is then proven by a committed read-back, not by a read)

save/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.save: persist a NEW entity (null id / version), merge an existing one, inside a read-write transaction; the change is committed when the transaction ends, so a later request reads it. A non-null id whose row does not exist is merged, and the SOURCE's provider (Hibernate 5) INSERTED a new row with a newly generated id for it; the destination's (Hibernate 6.6+) merge throws OptimisticLockException instead. Port the source's effect: when the id is set but no row exists, persist it as new (the identifier generated, never the requested one); merge only a row that exists
save/1.source: https://docs.hibernate.org/orm/6.6/migration-guide/migration-guide.html#merge-versioned-deleted ("Previously, merging a detached entity resulted in a SQL insert whenever there was no matching row in the database ... An OptimisticLockException is now thrown"); https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/jpa/reference/jpa/entity-persistence.html (a null id or null non-primitive version is new and persisted, anything else is merged)
save/1.evidence: v31 (spring-petclinic-rest-legacy-v31, 2026-10-02): every captured create whose request carries an id answered 500 (StaleObjectStateException from <X>RepositoryImpl.save, 'id == null ? persist : merge') where the source answered 201 with a newly generated id

saveAll/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.saveAll: save each element as save/1 does (including its id-without-row case), in one transaction

delete/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.delete: remove the entity (merged first when detached; a detached entity that no longer exists is ignored) inside a read-write transaction; the removal is committed, cascades as the mapping declares

deleteById/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.deleteById: find by id and delete/1 it; a missing id is ignored (Spring Data 3) or raises EmptyResultDataAccessException (Spring Data 2) -- the source's own version decides

deleteAll/0.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.deleteAll: delete/1 every entity, in one transaction

findAll/0.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.findAll: every entity of the domain type, read-only transaction

findById/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.findById: the entity with that id; the declared return type decides Optional vs nullable

findAllById/1.semantics: SimpleJpaRepository.findAllById: the entities with those ids

query_result_semantics.single_entity: Spring Data JPA returns null when a query method declared with a single entity (not Optional, not a collection) finds no row -- a @Query, a derived query or findById on the repository -- and raises IncorrectResultSizeDataAccessException for more than one. JPA's TypedQuery.getSingleResult() throws NoResultException for no row, which answers 500 where the source answered its own null path (typically 404). Port the member as query.getResultStream().findFirst().orElse(null) when the source guarantees at most one row (an id or unique key), or catch NoResultException and return null; never getSingleResult() bare, and never turn the source's null into an exception or an empty object
query_result_semantics.optional: an Optional return is Optional.empty() for no row (getResultStream().findFirst())
query_result_semantics.collection: a collection return is an empty collection for no row (getResultList())

persistence_behaviour_translations.note: Behaviour a LITERAL port of source persistence code does not preserve on the destination's persistence provider (V17-3). Each row is matched against the ORDERED calls the frozen structural model records for the selected source method (owner type and method name, pre-order); a match adds an obligation to that owed member: port the BEHAVIOUR (the committed effects the source produced), not the text. hibernate6-flush-before-query.obligation: the source removes the entity and THEN queries or bulk-deletes its dependents. Hibernate 6 (the destination's ORM) flushes the pending removal before an AUTO-flush query or a native/bulk statement runs, as the source's provider did for the captured scenarios. Port the COMMITTED EFFECTS THE SOURCE PRODUCED, scenario by scenario, never a reordering that changes them: where the source's delete SUCCEEDED (the row and its dependents gone), the destination's must too; where the source REFUSED it (a row still referenced: the constraint violation the flushed removal raised answered an error and the row stayed), the destination must refuse it the same way and keep the row -- never delete or detach the dependents first to make a refused delete succeed. Reorder only where the literal order fails on the destination (TransientPropertyValueException) for a delete the source completed; the check is the committed state the source recorded for each of its scenarios (the delete and the refused-delete scenarios alike)

build_plugins.note: Build plugins that GENERATE the destination's sources, and what their documented generators do to a request body (H7). A request body type that lives under target/generated-sources is owned by its generator's configuration in pom.xml, never by the controller: the planner (worklist.generated_body_binding) reads the generated type's constructor from the compiler model, compares the properties it requires with the recorded request body, and cites the row here. Rows are documentation from the generator's official reference; each option is quoted with its documented description and default. Nothing here is inferred from a specimen.

org.openapitools:openapi-generator-maven.option_location: a generator option goes under <configuration><configOptions><NAME>VALUE</NAME></configOptions> of the plugin (or of the execution that runs the generator)

jaxrs-spec.models: a model class gets a @JsonCreator constructor whose parameters carry @JsonProperty(required = true) for every property the spec's schema lists under `required` (generateJsonCreator, default true); Jackson then refuses a body that lacks one of those keys before any handler runs (a 400 at the boundary). The `spring` generator (library spring-boot) the legacy build used binds models through setters, so the same body was accepted there.

required_args_constructor.description: Whether to generate @JsonCreator constructor for required properties.

related_options.description: Whether to generate builders for models
whether to generate a constructor for all arguments
whether to use Jakarta EE namespace instead of javax
library template (sub-template) to use: <default> (JAXRS spec only, to be deployed in an app server), quarkus, thorntail, openliberty, helidon, kumuluzee

jaxrs-spec.action: set <generateJsonCreator>false</generateJsonCreator> under the plugin's <configOptions> in pom.xml (the generator then emits no required-args @JsonCreator constructor and the model binds through its setters, as the spring generator's did) and keep <useBeanValidation>true</useBeanValidation> (the model's constraints are what the handler validates); leave the spec's `required` lists as they are unless the source's contract does not require the property either. Do not edit the generated file (the next build rewrites it) and do not touch the controller for this difference.
jaxrs-spec.observation: a @ControllerAdvice/@ExceptionHandler that turns the deserialization failure into a body in the source is a separate concern: the destination's platform answers the boundary refusal itself, and whether a mapper renders a body is a build-profile/mapping question, not this obligation's.
jaxrs-spec.when: a conditional rule (V16-8): the request body type is generated by this generator, its generated @JsonCreator constructor (or, while target/ is stale, the spec's `required` list) requires a property the source's recorded request does not send, and the pom does not already set generateJsonCreator=false. Then the item is a PARITY_GENERATED_BODY build obligation on pom.xml and this row's action is its FIRST ACTION.

useBeanValidation.why: the model's constraints (@NotNull, @Size, nested @Valid) are what the handler's validator reads; generateJsonCreator only removes the required-args constructor, a container property stays initialized to an empty list, so the constraint on it still holds for a body that omits it

A recipe fixes WHAT the repair is and HOW it is accepted; it is never a second transformation engine. `implementation.kind` is `decided-repairs` (a mechanical operation of bootstrap-destination/scripts/_decided_repairs.py, applied only when decisions.yaml decided_repairs names it, with a receipt row), `agent-bounded` (an M3 worker edits inside the issued write grant; the selected architecture is the cited catalog row and the acceptance checks below are mechanical) or `typed-repair` (V26-1: `operation` is a recipe of the pinned harness executor fix-until-green/typed-repair (pins.typed_repair, OpenRewrite LST, typed references only); brief.py renders `typed-repair.py --root . --cluster <id>` as the issued unit's FIRST ACTION, the executor stages the complete patch inside the issued write grant and records applied | already-in-required-form | not-applicable | unresolved | failed; `covers` names what it edits and `fallback` is the bounded agent procedure an unresolved result returns to, with its reason; the edit is judged by the same acceptance checks as an agent-authored one and a no-op establishes nothing). `acceptance` names the EXISTING independent checks that refuse the recipe's known broken forms: a check a recipe names must exist (source_requirements.test.py resolves every checker and every package-level test). `applies_to` keys are qualified catalog identities; `refuse` lists the conditions under which the requirement stays unresolved and no edit is made. A recipe never widens a write set and never discharges another requirement (the retirement of an adapter-owned annotation discharges no adapter behaviour).

objective_families.note: Compatibility objectives (planner.compatibility_objectives, policy compatibility-objectives/v1, decisions.loop.compatibility_objectives). A family is ONE named change to an application contract; its transformations list the qualified symbols (a package and the types it exports are aliases of one transformation) or the MTA rules it retires, and its requirement_rules the source requirements that belong to that change. Admitted units of one family that share a site (the same file, for symbol families; the same rule, for rule families) compose into ONE bounded executable scope; independent components stay separate; a unit no family names stays its own objective. Composition is judged by these rows and qualified source facts only -- never by a layer, a file name or a package spelling. Borrowed from OpenRewrite/Moderne: small transformations composed into a larger one where partial application cannot meet the checkpoint (https://docs.openrewrite.org/concepts-and-explanations/recipes), applicability decided before editing (https://docs.openrewrite.org/reference/yaml-format-reference), and coupled incompatible changes applied together (https://docs.moderne.io/hands-on-learning/spring-boot-migration/module-6-wave-migration/). No recipe engine is run.
